bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42491774 (c-blosc2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target decompress_frame_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42491774
bug_description.normalized: The staged 89-byte witness first enters project logic when `blosc2_frame_from_sframe` decodes bytes 16..23 as `frame_len = 89`; because that matches `len` and the trailer marker check also passes, `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe` keeps a direct alias of the attacker buffer in `frame->sdata`. `blosc2_frame_to_schunk` then parses the same header bytes into absurd but positive internal sizes: `nbytes = 0x00fffff6010b0097` and `chunksize = 0x6b29ce00`, which make `get_header_info` derive `schunk->nchunks = 40078691`. On the reproduced 32-bit build, the harness casts that 64-bit `schunk->nbytes` to `size_t`, truncating it to `17498263`; the explicit `+1` in `malloc((size_t)schunk->nbytes + 1)` then makes the allocation request `17498264`, so `uncompressed_data` is non-NULL and the first decompression attempt for `nchunk = 0` executes. During that first `frame_get_lazychunk` call, `get_header_info` reparses `header_len = -197` and `cbytes = 0x0000850000000062`; `get_coffsets` uses those untrusted values directly in the in-memory path and returns `frame->sdata + header_len + cbytes` with no bounds check. That derived pointer lies 146235046494109 bytes past the 89-byte buffer, `get_coffset` passes it to `blosc_getitem` as if it were a valid compressed offsets chunk, and `blosc_getitem` immediately crashes on the first header-byte read at `_src[BLOSC2_CHUNK_VERSION]`, matching the saved ASan stack `blosc_getitem -> get_coffset -> frame_get_lazychunk -> frame_decompress_chunk`.

source.description: The first project-side read of the fuzz input decodes the outer serialized-frame length from bytes 16..23. For the staged witness it yields `frame_len = 89`, and that value immediately feeds the `frame_len != len` admission check that decides whether the buffer will be treated as a Blosc2 frame.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness passes the staged 89-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42491774/poc` (sha256 `3567ec75025e34fb5edccb1dde2c86c293f86da306548cced27b5ba8ec0ca17f`) straight to `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe((uint8_t *)data, size)` at `tests/fuzz/fuzz_decompress_frame.c:23`. Under the vulnerable frame layout, bytes 16..23 decode to `frame_len = 89`, matching `size`, and byte 66 is `0xce`, so `blosc2_frame_from_sframe` continues to the no-copy alias. Later reparses of the same buffer read bytes 11..14 as `header_len = -197`, bytes 30..37 as `nbytes = 0x00fffff6010b0097`, bytes 39..46 as `cbytes = 0x0000850000000062`, and bytes 53..56 as `chunksize = 0x6b29ce00`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `blosc_getitem` treats the out-of-range `coffsets` pointer as the start of a Blosc chunk and immediately reads its version byte, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1` at `blosc/blosc2.c:2404:21` with stack `blosc_getitem -> get_coffset -> frame_get_lazychunk -> frame_decompress_chunk -> blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and explicitly says the address is a wild pointer.

root_cause.description: The in-memory `get_coffsets` path trusts the attacker-derived `header_len` and `cbytes` fields as a byte offset into `frame->sdata` and returns that pointer without checking that the computed location stays inside the serialized frame buffer.
root_cause.note: For the staged witness, the reparsed values are `header_len = -197` and `cbytes = 146235046494306`, so `header_len + cbytes = 146235046494109` and the returned `coffsets` pointer is far outside the 89-byte `sframe` object before `get_coffset` hands it to `blosc_getitem`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the set of internal frame lengths decoded directly from the aliased attacker buffer. `get_header_info` reads `header_len`, `nbytes`, `cbytes`, and `chunksize` out of `frame->sdata` with no coherence check, and those values later drive both the huge chunk count and the wild offsets pointer.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness passes the outer serialized-frame checks in `blosc2_frame_from_sframe`: bytes 16..23 decode to `frame_len = 89`, which matches the actual file length, and the trailer marker check at line 786 also succeeds because byte 66 is `0xce`. Execution therefore reaches line 799 and keeps the input buffer as `frame->sdata`.

coarse_trace.summary: `blosc2_frame_from_sframe` decodes the outer `frame_len` from the 89-byte witness, its admission checks pass, and `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe` keeps a direct in-memory alias of the attacker buffer in `frame->sdata`.
The same aliased bytes are parsed as corrupted internal lengths; `nbytes` and `chunksize` are both positive, so `get_header_info` derives a huge positive `schunk->nchunks`.

On the reproduced 32-bit build, the harness truncates `schunk->nbytes` to the 32-bit `size_t` value `17498263`, the explicit `+1` makes `malloc` request `17498264` bytes, and the non-NULL buffer lets the first `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` call execute because `schunk->nchunks - 1` is still positive.

While fetching chunk 0, the frame parser reparses `header_len` and `cbytes` from the same input and the in-memory `get_coffsets` path computes a `coffsets` pointer far beyond the 89-byte frame by returning `frame->sdata + header_len + cbytes` without bounds validation.
`get_coffset` passes that wild `coffsets` pointer to `blosc_getitem` as if it were a valid compressed offsets chunk, and `blosc_getitem` crashes on its first header-byte read.

fine_trace.note: The first project-side read of the fuzzer buffer decodes bytes 16..23 into `frame_len = 89`. That attacker-controlled outer length is then compared against `len` to decide whether the serialized input will be accepted as a frame at all.

After step 0 makes `frame_len = 89`, the following `if (frame_len != len)` check does not reject the input; the trailer marker at line 786 is also `0xce`, and because `copy` is false the open-sframe path keeps a direct alias of the attacker buffer in `frame->sdata` instead of copying it. All later header parses and pointer arithmetic use this alias.

During `blosc2_frame_to_schunk`, the caller passes `&schunk->nbytes`, so this header read materializes the attacker-controlled 64-bit value `schunk->nbytes = 0x00fffff6010b0097` (72057551105753239) from the aliased frame bytes.
The same parse reads `schunk->chunksize = 0x6b29ce00` (1797901824), a positive divisor that will be combined with step 2 to derive how many chunks the harness believes the frame contains.

Using the values from steps 2 and 3, `get_header_info` computes `40078691` chunks. Because `blosc2_frame_to_schunk` passed `&schunk->nchunks`, this huge positive count becomes persistent super-chunk metadata instead of being rejected as inconsistent with the 89-byte frame.
On the reproduced 32-bit build, the cast inside the `malloc` expression truncates `schunk->nbytes = 0x00fffff6010b0097` to the 32-bit `size_t` value `17498263` before the explicit `+1` is applied.

The explicit `+1` turns the truncated size from step 5 into a `17498264`-byte allocation request. The saved execution reaches the later decompression stack, so this `malloc` returned a non-NULL `uncompressed_data` buffer and the guarded loop body remained reachable.

fine_trace.code:
for (i = 0, nchunk = 0; nchunk < schunk->nchunks-1; nchunk++) {
  dsize = blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk(schunk, nchunk, uncompressed_data + i, schunk->chunksize);
fine_trace.note: The loop starts with `nchunk = 0`, and step 4 made `schunk->nchunks - 1` positive (`40078690`), so the first `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` call is taken instead of returning early.

When `frame_get_lazychunk` begins handling chunk 0, it reparses the same aliased frame bytes and materializes `header_len = -197`, a negative base offset that should not be accepted as the start of a valid offsets area.

The same reparsing step also reads `cbytes = 0x0000850000000062` (146235046494306), a huge positive compressed-data length that is inconsistent with the 89-byte input but still forwarded to later pointer arithmetic.

Because this is an in-memory frame (`frame->sdata != NULL`), `get_coffsets` takes the direct pointer path and adds the attacker-controlled values from steps 8 and 9 to the aliased buffer base from step 1. The resulting pointer is `sframe + 146235046494109`, far outside the 89-byte object, and there is no check that `header_len >= 0`, `cbytes >= 0`, or `header_len + cbytes <= frame->len` before returning it.

On the first loop iteration `nchunk` is 0, so `get_coffset` asks `blosc_getitem` for the first 64-bit chunk offset. It passes the wild `coffsets` pointer from step 10 as if it were a valid compressed offsets chunk, and `blosc_getitem` has no actual source-length argument here to revalidate that memory before touching it.

The first statement in `blosc_getitem` dereferences the wild pointer received in step 11 as though it were the start of a chunk header. AddressSanitizer reports this exact 1-byte read as the crashing heap-buffer-overflow and identifies the address as a wild pointer.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, and `reproduction_report.json`; Stage 02 did not run fixed-version dynamic validation

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42491774 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/decompress_frame_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `blosc_getitem` with stack `get_coffset -> frame_get_lazychunk -> frame_decompress_chunk`.

format.name: 89-byte in-memory Blosc2 sframe with coherent outer frame length but corrupt internal header lengths
format.contract: Exactly the staged 89-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42491774/poc` (sha256 `3567ec75025e34fb5edccb1dde2c86c293f86da306548cced27b5ba8ec0ca17f`). The outer frame wrapper must satisfy the two checks in `blosc2_frame_from_sframe`: bytes 16..23 decode to `frame_len = 89`, matching the file length, and the trailer marker byte at offset 66 is `0xce`. The same witness must also decode under the vulnerable frame layout to `header_len = -197` (bytes 11..14), `nbytes = 0x00fffff6010b0097` (bytes 30..37), `cbytes = 0x0000850000000062` (bytes 39..46), and `chunksize = 0x6b29ce00` (bytes 53..56). Those exact values are what make `get_header_info` derive `schunk->nchunks = 40078691`, make the 32-bit cast `(size_t)schunk->nbytes` truncate to `17498263`, make the explicit `+1` request `malloc` size `17498264`, and then make `get_coffsets` return `frame->sdata + header_len + cbytes`, a wild pointer that `get_coffset` passes to `blosc_getitem`.
